display.purpose: All headings via the base h1-h6 rule; see the Broken Heading Rule for the font-heading (Nunito Sans) caveat — that utility is applied to ~77% of real headings but the font is never loaded, so those instances silently fall back to system sans-serif instead of Fredoka.

body.purpose: Default body copy and most UI text, set on the <body> element.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover/interactive elevation, paired with a -translate-y lift.

shadows.name: btn
shadows.purpose: Resting shadow on primary/secondary pill buttons.

shadows.name: navbar
shadows.purpose: Hairline separator under the fixed public navbar.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action pill button (e.g. form submits, booking confirm).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #1D4073; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; border: none; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px 0 rgba(36,79,140,0.20); transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #16315A; transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px #4E79A2; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: High-emphasis gold CTA — used sparingly, one per screen (Sparing Gold Rule).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #FCC019; color: #003773; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; border: none; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px 0 rgba(252,192,25,0.25); transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #FDD65C; transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fff, 0 0 0 4px #FDD65C; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Lower-emphasis secondary action alongside a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 19px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #fff; color: #244F8C; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; border: 2px solid #244F8C; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #E9EEF4; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Standard pill text input with a visible resting border.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #fff; color: #1B1C1C; font-size: 14px; border: 2px solid #C3C6D1; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #434750; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #4E79A2; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #E9EEF4; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Small status/category pill; each variant is a same-hue 50/700 tint pair (Tinted-Pair Badge Rule).
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; background: #E9EEF4; color: #1D4073; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Base raised surface — white, soft blue-tinted shadow, generous radius.
components.html:
Maria Silva

Petsitter em Cuiabá — 4.9 ★ (32 avaliações)
components.css: .ds-card { background: #fff; border-radius: 24px; padding: 24px; box-shadow: 0 1px 4px 0 rgba(36,79,140,0.06), 0 4px 16px 0 rgba(36,79,140,0.06); transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Fredoka', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; color: #1B1C1C; margin: 0 0 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 14px; color: #434750; margin: 0; }

components.name: Toggle Switch
components.description: iOS-style on/off switch used in settings/preferences.
components.css: .ds-toggle { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 28px; width: 48px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #C3C6D1; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; padding: 0; } .ds-toggle[data-state='on'] { background: #244F8C; } .ds-toggle-thumb { display: inline-block; height: 20px; width: 20px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.15); transform: translateX(4px); transition: transform 0.2s; } .ds-toggle[data-state='on'] .ds-toggle-thumb { transform: translateX(24px); }

components.name: Ambient Blobs
components.description: Signature decorative background device: three blurred pulsing color orbs behind auth/match-wizard content.
components.css: .ds-blobs { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -10; overflow: hidden; pointer-events: none; } .ds-blob { position: absolute; border-radius: 9999px; filter: blur(64px); animation: ds-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-blob-1 { top: -96px; left: -96px; height: 288px; width: 288px; background: rgba(167,188,209,0.4); } .ds-blob-2 { top: 33%; right: -80px; height: 256px; width: 256px; background: rgba(242,223,167,0.4); animation-delay: 1s; } .ds-blob-3 { bottom: -96px; left: 25%; height: 320px; width: 320px; background: rgba(211,221,232,0.5); animation-delay: 2s; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%,100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.6; } }

narrative.overview:
PetUno's visual system does one specific job: make a tutor comfortable leaving their pet with a stranger they met through an app. That's a trust problem before it's a marketplace problem, and the design solves it by pairing an institutional, dependable blue with a warm, cheerful gold — then softening every edge in the interface until nothing reads as a logistics dashboard. Every button, input, badge, and nav item is pill-shaped (rounded-pill, 9999px); cards are large and gently rounded (24-32px); backgrounds carry blurred organic blobs instead of hard geometric decoration. The result reads as a professional service you'd trust with your dog, not a corporate SaaS panel and not a cartoon.

The pairing is deliberate: Deep Trust Blue grounds the system as the structural, dependable color (navbars, primary actions, headings-on-dark), while Golden Cheer is used sparingly as the "look here" color — CTAs, active states, ratings, the one badge that matters. Confirmed anti-reference: PetUno should never read as cold, clinical, or corporate — no sharp corners, no flat enterprise-blue panels, no hard black shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Pill-shaped everything: buttons, inputs, badges, chips, nav links, toggle switches.
Soft, blue-tinted ambient shadows — never pure black, never sharp-edged.
Organic blurred blob shapes and floating blurred orbs as background texture on hero, auth, and match surfaces.
Deep Trust Blue as structure/trust; Golden Cheer as sparing accent/action color.
Warm neutral canvas (#FBF9F8), not clinical white-on-white.

rules.name: The Solid Icon Badge Rule
rules.body: A small icon badge (~40-48px circle) needs a solid, saturated background (bg-primary-500) with a text-white icon, not a pale tint pair (bg-primary-100/text-primary-700) — at icon scale a thin-stroke icon on a low-chroma pale circle reads as washed out even when it technically passes a contrast checker.

rules.name: The Explicit White Heading Rule
rules.body: @layer base hardcodes h1-h6 { color: #1B1C1C } directly on the element selector. A parent's text-white does not cascade past this — every heading on a dark or colored section background needs its own explicit text-white class or it silently renders as near-black ink.

rules.name: The Sparing Gold Rule
rules.body: Golden Cheer marks the one action or state that should win the eye on a given screen. If more than one element on a screen competes in gold, the hierarchy has broken down.

rules.name: The Tinted-Pair Badge Rule
rules.body: Every badge variant is a {color}-50 background with {color}-700 text of the same hue family. Follow the existing hue family for a new badge variant; don't introduce a new tint formula.

rules.name: The Broken Heading Rule (fix before extending)
rules.body: font-heading is configured to Nunito Sans and applied to ~77% of headings, but Nunito Sans is never loaded, so those headings silently fall back to system sans-serif instead of Fredoka. Don't add new font-heading usages until this is resolved.

rules.name: The No-Black-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in the system is tinted with the brand blue's rgba (rgba(36,79,140, …)), never neutral black.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: Every interactive control is fully pill-shaped: buttons, inputs, badges, chips, nav links, the iOS-style toggle switch. This is the single most load-bearing shape decision in the system.

rules.name: The Gradient Wave Rule
rules.body: A wave divider's path fill is a linearGradient running from the current section's background color to the next section's, never a flat fill matching only the next color. The svg needs an explicit block class (inline SVGs reserve baseline whitespace like the classic gap-under-an-image bug, showing a stray pale seam line); the wrapper div needs a solid fallback bg-* matching the next section's color as a safety net for any residual sub-pixel gap.

dos: Do give every heading placed on a dark or colored section background its own explicit text-white class, per the Explicit White Heading Rule — never rely on inheritance from a parent.
Do keep every interactive control pill-shaped (rounded-pill). A rectangular or barely-rounded button/input is the clearest possible off-brand signal in this system.
Do treat Golden Cheer as scarce — one CTA or active state per screen, per the Sparing Gold Rule.
Do tint shadows with the brand blue's rgba, never plain black, per the No-Black-Shadow Rule.
Do use Trust Blue Deep (#003773) as text on Golden Cheer surfaces — the system's established high-contrast pairing.
Do use organic blob shapes or the AmbientBlobs component when a surface needs decorative background warmth.
donts: Don't design anything that reads as cold, clinical, or corporate-SaaS — that's PetUno's explicitly confirmed anti-reference.
Don't build against dark: variants or reintroduce darkMode: 'class' in tailwind.config.ts without a deliberate decision to support a dark theme — PetUno is light-only by design.
Don't add more font-heading usage without first resolving the Broken Heading Rule.
Don't introduce a new badge tint formula — follow the Tinted-Pair Badge Rule.
